subject: Velora Health — post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Velora Health — post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion. Per our demo, I captured a short performance-focused recap and the SLO checklist so the team can validate readiness for a pilot. Attaching the checklist (velora_slo_checklist.xlsx).

High-level recap / ask:
- Target SLOs you called out: p95 latency <= 200ms for ~256-token responses, sustained throughput ~250 req/s, peak concurrency target 80 concurrent sessions.
- Streaming: you require partial tokens delivered every ~50-100ms (low-latency streaming) for UI snappiness and progressive rendering.
- Fallback policy: must gracefully degrade to a smaller model (lower cost variant) when capacity constrained; fallbacks should preserve structure and token correctness.

Immediate next steps (proposed MAP):
1) Velora to provide a representative sample workload (we discussed the anonymized traffic trace) and a latency profile export — CloudOps for that.
2) Redwood to run an initial scale test (hosted + dedicated baseline) and share results and tuning guidance.
3) Agree acceptance criteria (pass/fail thresholds) and schedule canary window for a pilot.
4) Introduce procurement/legal contacts to discuss contract/SLAs if results look good.

Open questions we flagged that we can deliver answers on in the scale test:
- Can we meet p95 <= 200ms at concurrency 80 under the sample workload?
- Streaming chunk size tradeoffs vs throughput (how chunk size impacts CPU/GPU scheduling).
- Quantization/precision recommendations to hit your latency target without quality regressions.

Proposed timing: initial scale test week of Jan 25 (can adjust based on your procurement timeline).

Attachments: velora_slo_checklist.xlsx (SLO matrix + test plan stub).

Thanks — copying Ben and Karthik to get them involved on the test planning and execution.

--

Thanks Grace — this is very helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying points from our side:

1) The p95=200ms is our aspiration for interactive UI flows (average payload ~220-300 tokens). For longer completions (>=1k tokens) we expect higher latency; we'll capture that in the workload sample.
2) Streaming: we need partial output every ~80ms on the average user session. If that requires a tradeoff with throughput, please highlight the impact.
3) Quantization: are you able to run int8 or similar without losing the quality we showed in the demo? We can run a small eval set if you recommend it.

Provisional timeline: procurement + legal aim to be ready by mid-February. We will get the CloudOps team to send over the anonymized latency profile (attached).

Attachment: velora_internal_latency_profile.csv

Also, for the scale test, please include a clear pass/fail definition so our infra team knows when to greenlight a pilot.

Appreciate the quick follow-up.

—Emily

Subject: Re: Velora Health — post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Emily — thanks for the detail. Quick responses and a proposed plan from engineering side: 

- Quantization: we can support int8 quantization for many of the open model variants we demoed. We'll include a small eval comparing int8 vs fp16 on fidelity for your representative prompts.
- Streaming vs throughput: streaming with small chunk sizes increases scheduling overhead; our recommendation is 128-token streaming chunks as a starting point (good latency without excessive packetization). We'll measure 80ms chunk cadence during the test and share tradeoffs.
- Meeting p95 at concurrency 80: depends on model selection and whether you want hosted vs dedicated. We propose a two-path test: hosted baseline + dedicated GPU pool baseline (dedicated will give predictability).

Proposed MAP (attached as velora_map_v1.pdf):
1) You provide sample workload and auth to run scale tests (CloudOps).
2) We run baseline tests (hosted) and a dedicated run with autoscale rules.
3) Tuning: caching KV prefixes, batching knobs, and quantization experiment.
4) Acceptance decision: define pass/fail and then canary rollout plan.

I'll coordinate with Karthik on acceptance criteria and test scripts. Grace — can you confirm Jan 25 availability for a test window if Velora's infra can provide the trace by Jan 20?

--
Ben Carter

ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Velora Health — post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks — I outlined a pragmatic acceptance criteria set below (also attached as slo_acceptance_criteria.md). Please review and call out objections.

SLO acceptance (proposal):
- Baseline: hosted tests should achieve p95 <= 220ms for 512-token responses on the sample workload.
- Target: dedicated deployment should achieve p95 <= 180-200ms for the same workload.
- Throughput/concurrency: sustained throughput >= 250 req/s with observed 99th <= 2x p95 for the baseline run. Peak concurrency step test should succeed at 80 concurrent sessions for at least 10 minutes without errors.
- Streaming: partial-chunk latency <= 100ms 95% of the time with 128-token chunking.
- Quality guardrails: int8 quantized model must not degrade quality on an eval set beyond a small, pre-agreed delta (we'll run that during tests).

Test plan highlights:
1) Two-phase load test: increasing concurrency steps (10/25/50/80), 15 mins each, capture p50/p95/p99, error rates, and memory/GPU metrics.
2) Fallback simulation: reduce capacity mid-run to validate fallback to cheaper model and verify response correctness.
3) Canary plan: 10% traffic for 6 hours -> 50% for 24 hours -> full, with automated rollback on SLO regressions.

If this looks good I'll prepare the exact test harness and the scripts we will run. Suggested acceptance threshold for go/no-go to pilot: dedicated p95 <= 200ms and no unexplained error spike (>0.5% error rate).

Attachments: slo_acceptance_criteria.md

-Karthik
